text.p: - The supervisory board of the country's third largest commercial bank, Investicna a Rozvojova Banka (IRB) a.s., has replaced the bank's board of directors.
- The paper publishes a series of recommendations by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for sustaining the country's macroeconomic stability in the comming years.
- The Slovak government is preparing an amendment to the law on the National Bank of Slovakia in order to harmonise the country's monetary and fiscal policies.

- The Party of the Democratic Left, the former communists, will propose a law banning the privatisation of the banking sector following calls by the Slovak Workers Party for extension of a privatisation moratorium until the year 2008.
- A Prague Capital Partners-led investment group has reqested an extraordinary general meeting of Jacobs Suchard Figaro a.s. to improve the company's information policy towards its shareholders.
- Slovenska Posta s.p. is considering a 400 million crown five-year bond issue with a 12-13.5 percent coupon in April through Postova Banka a.s..
- Tabloid Novy Cas continues to be Slovakia's most-read daily with 31 percent readership, followed with a 13 percent share for left-wing Pravda and nine-percent share for Sport.
- Pharmaceuticals producer Slovakofarma a.s. posted an after-tax profit of 678 million crowns in 1996, some 150 million higher than the previous year.
